title: Conditioning away interactions keeps the original coordinate access contract
statement: For independent known coordinate laws and square-integrable node/pair target on graph G, firstread a supplied/acquired vertex cover H. Remaining contributions are independent one-coordinate functions; read up to k with largest CONDITIONAL variance. This dominates every original HARD-k adaptive coordinate policy using at mostmin(n,|H|+k)reads and only second moments. A maximal matching gives a2-approximate cover inO(n+|E|); applicable bipartite algorithms are ordinary controls. On rare-gate family, m gates form a cover and3m total reads dominate hard-2m, with risk tending to exp(-1) versus fixed-3m risk tending to 1; at m=20 the reported risks are.351713versus optimal fixed-60 risk.925641. The naive EXPECTED-budget extension fails because favorable first-stage outcomes can justify many more reads; global conditional-variance thresholding needs separately paid integration over H outcomes. No Gaussian/programmed-linear access is smuggled into this companion.
